2026 Three layers of protection LAYER 1 · ARTICLE 21 Privacy and dignity Morphed sexual content violates privacy and dignity even if no one profits from it. LAYER 2 · COPYRIGHT ACT, S. 38B Performer's moral rights Protects the integrity of a performance, separate from who owns the economic rights. LAYER 3 · PUBLICITY Commercial value of identity A recognisable persona has economic value that others can't take without consent. Under this framework, financial loss doesn't have to be proved. Adv. OPEN QUESTIONS Where is the line? Parody and commentary Courts say free speech protects critique and commentary, but not commercial exploitation of a persona. Satire of public figures is not yet clearly carved out. Not every name is protected Deverakonda was refused an ex parte injunction over the nickname "Rowdy": secondary meaning wasn't yet shown. Ex parte, interim, early Most orders are interim and made without hearing the other side. Arjun Kapoor's final decree is a rare full decision. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 06 / 08

IF YOU ARE NOT A CELEBRIT Y What can an ordinary person do? Report the content to the platform's grievance officer under the IT Rules, and escalate to the Grievance Appellate Committee if needed File a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in or call the 1930 helpline Under the IT Rules 2026, platforms must take down unlawful synthetic content within 3 hours of a court or government order Approach the court for an injunction based on privacy and dignity (Article 21); being famous isn't required Preserve evidence first: URLs, screenshots with dates, account names Adv. TA K E AWAY Judges are writing the law that Parliament hasn't. Court-made protection is moving fast, but it is uneven and mostly interim. India needs a clear statutory right that protects everyone's face and voice, not only celebrities'. Adv.
